system.biography:
The tarrasque is 70 feet long and 50 feet tall, and it weighs about 130 tons.

The tarrasque cannot speak.

Combat

The tarrasque attacks with its claws, teeth, horns, and tail.

The tarrasque’s natural weapons are treated as epic weapons for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction.

Augmented Critical (Ex)

The tarrasque’s bite threatens a critical hit on a natural attack roll of 18-20, dealing triple damage on a successful critical hit.

Frightful Presence (Su)

The tarrasque can inspire terror by charging or attacking. Affected creatures must succeed on a DC 36 Will save or become shaken, remaining in that condition as long as they remain with 60 feet of the tarrasque. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Improved Grab (Ex)

To use this ability, the tarrasque must hit a Huge or smaller opponent with its bite attack. It can then attempt to start a grapple as a free action without provoking an attack of opportunity. If it wins the grapple check, it establishes a hold and can try to swallow the foe the following round.

Rush (Ex)

Once per minute, the normally slow-moving tarrasque can move at a speed of 150 feet.

Swallow Whole (Ex)

The tarrasque can try to swallow a grabbed opponent of Huge or smaller size by making a successful grapple check. Once inside, the opponent takes 2d8+8 points of crushing damage plus 2d8+6 points of acid damage per round from the tarrasque’s digestive juices. A swallowed creature can cut its way out by dealing 50 points of damage to the tarrasque’s digestive tract (AC 25). Once the creature exits, muscular action closes the hole; another swallowed opponent must cut its own way out. The tarrasque’s gullet can hold 2 Huge, 8 Large, 32 Medium, 128 Small, or 512 Tiny or smaller creatures.

Carapace (Ex)

The tarrasque’s armorlike carapace is exceptionally tough and highly reflective, deflecting all rays, lines, cones, and even magic missile spells. There is a 30% chance of reflecting any such effect back at the caster; otherwise, it is merely negated. Check for reflection before rolling to overcome the creature’s spell resistance.

Regeneration (Ex)

No form of attack deals lethal damage to the tarrasque. The tarrasque regenerates even if it fails a saving throw against a disintegrate spell or a death effect. If the tarrasque fails its save against a spell or effect that would kill it instantly (such as those mentioned above), the spell or effect instead deals nonlethal damage equal to the creature’s full normal hit points +10 (or 868 hp). The tarrasque is immune to effects that produce incurable or bleeding wounds, such as mummy rot, a sword with the wounding special ability, or a clay golem’s cursed wound ability.

The tarrasque can be slain only by raising its nonlethal damage total to its full normal hit points +10 (or 868 hit points) and using a wish or miracle spell to keep it dead.

If the tarrasque loses a limb or body part, the lost portion regrows in 1d6 minutes (the detached piece dies and decays normally). The creature can reattach the severed member instantly by holding it to the stump.

Skills

The tarrasque has a +8 racial bonus on Listen and Spot checks.

system.description: You are particularly observant.
system.benefit: You get a +2 bonus on all Listen checks and Spot checks.

system.description: As a standard action, the creature may choose to subtract 4 from its melee attack roll and deliver an awesome blow.
system.prerequisites: Str 25, Power Attack, Improved Bull Rush, size Large or larger
system.benefit: If the creature hits a Huge or smaller opponent with an awesome blow, the opponent must succeed on a Fortitude save (DC = damage dealt) or be knocked flying 10 feet in a direction of the attacker’s choice and fall prone.

system.description: You are skilled at fighting opponents you cannot clearly see.
system.benefit:
In melee, every time you miss because of concealment, you can reroll your miss chance percentile roll one time to see if you actually hit.

An invisible attacker gets no advantages related to hitting you in melee. That is, you don't lose your Dexterity bonus to Armor Class, and the attacker doesn't get the usual +2 bonus to hit you. The invisible attacker's bonuses do still apply for ranged attacks, however.

You take only half the usual penalty to speed for being unable to see. Darkness and poor visibility in general reduces your speed to three-quarters normal, instead of one-half.
system.special: A fighter may select Blind-Fight as one of his fighter bonus feats.

system.description: You can strike two adjacent foes with a single swing.
system.benefit: As a standard action, you can make a single attack at your full base attack bonus against a foe within reach. If you hit, you deal damage normally and can make an additional attack (using your full base attack bonus) against a foe that is adjacent to the first and also within reach. You can only make one additional attack per round with this feat. You cannot use this feat if you are wearing heavy armor.
system.special: A fighter may select Cleave as one of his fighter bonus feats.

system.description: You can make additional attacks of opportunity.
system.benefit: You may make a number of additional attacks of opportunity per round equal to your Dexterity bonus. With this feat, you may also make attacks of opportunity while flat-footed.

system.description: You are adept at dodging blows.
system.benefit: During your action, you designate an opponent and receive a +1 dodge bonus to Armor Class against attacks from that opponent. You can select a new opponent on any action.

system.description: You can strike many adjacent foes with a single swing.
system.prerequisites: Cleave, Power Attack, Str 13, base attack bonus +4
system.benefit: As a standard action, you can make a single attack at your full base attack bonus against a foe within reach. If you hit, you deal damage normally and can make an additional attack (using your full base attack bonus) against a foe that is adjacent to the first and also within reach. If you hit that foe, you can continue to make attacks against other adjacent foes so long as you keep hitting. You cannot attack an individual foe more than once per round with this feat. You cannot use this feat if you are wearing heavy armor.
system.special: A fighter may select Great Cleave as one of his fighter bonus feats.

system.description: You are skilled at pushing your opponents around.
system.benefit: When you perform a bull rush, you do not provoke an attack of opportunity from the defender. You also gain a +4 bonus on the opposed Strength check you make to push back the defender.
system.special: A fighter may select Improved Bull Rush as one of his fighter bonus feats.

system.description: You are exceptionally quick and alert.
system.benefit: You get a +4 bonus on initiative checks.

system.description: You have a stronger will than normal.
system.benefit: You get a +2 bonus on all Will saving throws.

system.description: You can make exceptionally powerful melee attacks.
system.benefit: On your action, before making attack rolls for a round, you may choose to subtract a number from all melee attack rolls and add the same number to all melee damage rolls. This number may not exceed your base attack bonus. The penalty on attacks and bonus on damage apply until your next turn.

system.description: You have enhanced physical stamina.
system.benefit: You gain +3 hit points. For every Hit Die beyond 3, you gain an additional +1 hit point. If you have more than 3 Hit Dice, you gain +1 hit points whenever you gain a Hit Die (such as when you gain a level).

system.description: Your Listen check is either made against a DC that reflects how quiet the noise is that you might hear, or it is opposed by the target's Move Silently check.
You can find secret doors, traps, and hidden objects.
Your Spot check is either made against a DC that reflects how obvious the object is, or it is opposed by the target's Hide check.
You are skilled at surviving in the wild and at following tracks.

What it does (SRD): Thick hide or similar quality gives damage reduction with no bypass (e.g. DR 2/—).

ThirdEra: Canonical template uses value 0 on the DR grant; set the real value under CGS parameters and overrides.

grants.label: Damage reduction (no bypass); value from overrides.

system.description: SRD: The creature is immune to fire.

What it does (SRD): Scent lets the creature detect opponents by smell, usually out to about 30 ft. (strong scents farther, very weak scents closer). It can use scent to pinpoint a square once it is within 5 ft., and to track by Survival. Wind and water affect what it can smell.

ThirdEra: Scent (30 ft.) is set on this item’s Details tab under Capability grants (vision and senses), not in Mechanical effects. The character sheet includes it with other senses; Survival checks to track by scent still use the normal skill rules unless you add separate bonuses elsewhere.

What it does (SRD): If the creature hits with a listed natural weapon, it can attempt to start a grapple as a free action without provoking attacks of opportunity. Details (size modifiers, opposed checks, holding vs pinning) follow the grapple rules.

ThirdEra: This template has no numeric rows in Mechanical effects or Capability grants. Track grapple state in play; use the NPC’s natural attacks and CMB/CMD from the sheet when resolving the grapple.

What it does (SRD): If the creature starts its turn with an opponent grappled in its mouth, it can swallow that opponent with another successful grapple check. Swallowed creatures can attack from inside, may be affected by acid or bludgeoning damage from the gizzard, and escape by cutting free or escaping the grapple.

ThirdEra: This item is prose-first: keep Mechanical effects and Capability grants empty unless you add a homebrew numeric row. Use the printed bite/gizzard damage, AC to cut out, and interior space from the stat block.

Carapace (Ex): Reflects magic missile and line spells; polymorph and petrification fail unless save DC is 20 higher than normal.

Regeneration (Ex): 40 per round; only epic damage overcomes regeneration (see SRD).

Frightful presence (Ex): 300-ft. radius; Will save or panicked (4d6 rounds shaken if HD exceeds the tarrasque's).

Augmented critical, rush: Per SRD tarrasque entry.

Immunities (SRD): Fire, poison, disease, energy drain, and ability damage (in addition to embedded immunities).

What it does (SRD): The creature is immune to disease unless a specific effect overrides immunity.

ThirdEra: On this item’s Details tab, the immunity is under Capability grants (immunity), not in Mechanical effects.

What it does (SRD): The creature is immune to poison: it does not take ability damage or hit point damage from poison, and it ignores other harmful poison effects unless a specific effect overrides immunity.

ThirdEra: On this item’s Details tab, poison immunity is under Capability grants (immunity), not as save or AC bonuses in Mechanical effects. The character sheet lists it with other immunities and defenses from the creature’s items and features.

What it does (SRD): The creature can see in total darkness out to the distance set on this copy (default from the stat block). Darkvision is black and white only unless another rule says otherwise.

ThirdEra: Distance is under CGS parameters and overrides on this item (merged over the canonical template). The stat block’s distance is preserved when migrating from older packs.
